name: Chen Liang
current_role: Actual controller of Weihai Guangwei Composites (SZSE: 300699) via Weihai Guangwei Group; former chairman (chairman is now Lu Zhaojun)
profile: Chen Liang (陈亮) is the second-generation controller of Weihai Guangwei Composites, a Shandong carbon-fibre maker that grew out of a fishing-rod business founded by Chen Guangwei. In 2021 he and his brother Chen Dong each received ~39.9% of parent Guangwei Group; since 2024 Chen Dong's votes are delegated to him, making him sole actual controller.
interesting_fact: Guangwei began as a fishing-tackle company using carbon composites in fishing rods, then pivoted into making China's own carbon fibre when foreign suppliers restricted products, technology and equipment.
deep_cut_fact: Under a March 6, 2024 concert-party agreement, his brother Chen Dong delegated all his Guangwei Group voting rights to Chen Liang, making him the listed company's sole actual controller (per the H1 2026 report).
notes: Low public profile; many unrelated people share the name 陈亮 (e.g. the CICC chairman), so don't mix them up. Best route is the company's board-secretary/IR contact. Deep-cut fact is corporate-governance detail rather than personal.

name: Morris S Young
current_role: Chairman (since Aug 2021) and CEO (since July 2009) of AXT, Inc. (Nasdaq: AXTI), Fremont, California
profile: Dr. Morris Young co-founded AXT in 1986. AXT makes indium phosphide, gallium arsenide and germanium substrate wafers, mostly in China via subsidiary Beijing Tongmei. He was president/CEO 1989-2004, returned as CEO in 2009 and became chairman in 2021. InP substrates for AI/data-center optical links have become AXT's key growth market.
interesting_fact: In Oct 2026 AXT's Beijing subsidiary Tongmei agreed a private equity raise of up to RMB 3.67bn (~US$545m) to expand indium phosphide substrate capacity, the material behind optical interconnects in AI data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding AXT, Young was a physicist at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (1985-89). He holds a B.S. in metallurgical engineering from National Cheng Kung University in Taiwan, an M.S. from Syracuse and a Ph.D. in metallurgy from Polytechnic University (now NYU Tandon).

public_contacts.value: Leslie Green, Green Communications Consulting, LLC - leslie@greencommunicationsllc.com (AXT investor relations)

notes: Highly relevant to the data-center theme because InP substrates go into AI optical transceivers. Best route is the IR agency (Leslie Green). The CFO line (510) 438-4700 is published in press releases.

name: Gu Yunkui
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2004-2016) as Gu Yunkui (顾云奎) of 'Jiangsu Yongding' (cable, real estate). Web searches in English and Chinese found no independent sources linking this name to a Yongding company. The best-known Jiangsu Yongding cable group (Yongding Co., SSE 600105) is publicly associated with the Mo family, not Gu.
notes: Identity could not be verified. The Hurun listing may be a transliteration or company-name error, and he has been off the list since 2016. Recommend deprioritising unless the journalist can confirm the person and company from the original Hurun entry.

name: Yuan Wenjie
current_role: Chairman and co-actual controller of Baotou Tianhe Magnetics Technology Co. (SSE: 603072)
profile: Yuan Wenjie (袁文杰) chairs Baotou Tianhe Magnetics, an Inner Mongolia maker of sintered NdFeB and SmCo rare-earth permanent magnets for EVs, wind turbines, efficient appliances and electronics. With his sons Yuan Bo and Yuan Yi, he controls about 70% of the company, which listed on the Shanghai main board in Jan 2025.
interesting_fact: Tianhe's revenue rose from RMB 1.15bn in 2020 to RMB 2.885bn in 2022 on demand for high-performance magnets for EV motors and wind power. The company is based in Baotou's rare-earth high-tech zone.
deep_cut_fact: According to the sponsor's IPO report, a technical team centred on Yuan Wenjie has been developing and producing sintered NdFeB magnets since 1993, nearly from the start of China's rare-earth permanent-magnet industry. The company itself was founded in 2008.
notes: Low media profile with no personal interviews found. He is relevant to the energy theme through magnets for wind turbines and EVs. Best route is the board secretary's office via the IR email. Not to be confused with a Dalian University of Technology professor of the same name.

name: Li Luyuan
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2016-2021) as Li Luyuan (李禄媛), with wealth from 'Jiankun' in the 'life service' sector. Searches in Chinese and English found no independent source tying this name to a company called Jiankun. The only 'Jiankun' found was Malaysia's Jiankun International Bhd, an unrelated property developer.
notes: Identity could not be verified and the person appears very private. Check the original Hurun entry for the company's full Chinese name before any outreach.

name: Deng Jieru
current_role: Actual controller and largest shareholder of Chengdu RML Technology (SZSE ChiNext: 301050); former executive (chairman is now Gui Jun)
profile: Deng Jieru (邓洁茹) is the ultimate controller of Chengdu RML Technology (雷电微力), a maker of millimetre-wave active phased-array microsystems used in radar, data links, guidance and satellite payloads. The company listed on ChiNext in Aug 2021. She holds about 19.3% directly and more through Wuhan Integrated Circuit Industry Technology Research Institute, which she ~94% owns. She has left her executive role.
interesting_fact: RML's products include satellite-borne and airborne millimetre-wave phased-array microsystems. The company was added to the US Commerce Department's Entity List in Jan 2025 and said this would not materially affect operations.
deep_cut_fact: She controls RML partly through a holding company named 'Wuhan Integrated Circuit Industry Technology Research Institute' (武汉集成电路工业技术研究院), which she owns 94.22%, according to RML's 2024 annual report.
notes: Very private, with no interviews found. The company is defence-oriented and on the US Entity List, which is sensitive for a podcast. She is no longer an executive, so the only route is via the company IR email.

name: Yu Tuliang
current_role: Vice chairman of Zhejiang Sun & Moon (Riyue) Jewelry Group; co-actual controller with his father Yu Awu of Zhejiang Ming Jewelry (SZSE: 002574)
profile: Yu Tuliang (虞兔良) and his father Yu Awu control Zhejiang Sun & Moon Jewelry Group, parent of listed gold-jewellery maker Zhejiang Ming Jewelry (明牌珠宝) in Shaoxing. He ran the business day to day as GM of the group (1995-2010) and as chairman and GM of Ming Jewelry (2009-2016). His father now chairs the listed company.
interesting_fact: Through Zhejiang Mingpai Industrial, the family's group holds 16.2% of Beijing Caishikou Department Store (Caibai, 605599), Beijing's famous gold and jewellery retailer, but has pledged not to take part in running it.
deep_cut_fact: He was chairman and general manager of Zhejiang Mingpai Industrial from 1999 to 2010, and from 2009 to 2016 chairman and GM of Ming Jewelry, which listed on the Shenzhen exchange in 2011.
notes: Hurun lists the wealth as shared with his father Yu Awu. Low media profile. The best route is the listed company's IR email. The business is jewellery and investments, with little overlap with energy or data-center topics.

name: Li Shilun
current_role: Director of Shaoxing Shangyu Jingsheng Investment (controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical, SZSE: 300316); retired Zhejiang University professor
profile: Li Shilun (李世伦), born 1962 and holding a PhD in engineering, spent 1988-2022 at Zhejiang University's School of Mechanical Engineering. He was part of the academic group behind Jingsheng M&E, which makes crystal-growth furnaces and equipment for solar and semiconductor silicon and SiC. His wealth comes from his stake in Jingsheng Investment, the controlling holding company.
interesting_fact: Jingsheng grew out of Zhejiang University's mechanical engineering school. Several founders and directors are ZJU professors, and it became one of China's main suppliers of monocrystalline silicon growth furnaces for the solar industry.
deep_cut_fact: He taught and did research at Zhejiang University's School of Mechanical Engineering for 34 years (Aug 1988-Jul 2022) before retiring. He was a Jingsheng director 2010-2015 and chaired its supervisory board from Dec 2019.
notes: Academic co-founder rather than an operator. He no longer appears among listed-company officers in the 2025 annual report, probably because China's 2024 Company Law changes led many firms to abolish supervisory boards. Highly relevant to the solar and semiconductor equipment theme. Route is via the company securities office.

name: Xu Bing
current_role: General manager of Guangzhou Zhanxin Communication Technology; co-actual controller (with Huang Shaoxiong) of Beijing Compass Technology (SZSE ChiNext: 300803)
profile: Xu Bing (徐兵) and Huang Shaoxiong control Compass Technology (指南针) through holding company Guangzhou Zhanxin. Compass is a Beijing-based retail stock-analysis software and fintech firm that listed on ChiNext in 2019 and has since moved into brokerage (Mega/麦高 Securities) and fund management. Xu has run Guangzhou Zhanxin since 2010.
interesting_fact: Compass grew from selling stock-analysis software to retail investors into a licensed financial group by acquiring a securities brokerage and a fund manager, using a software customer base to build a broker.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech, Xu served 1984-1997 in the Guangzhou Military Region Air Force logistics department, then worked 1997-2008 at Guangzhou Nanhu Golf Club (assistant GM, later director), according to Compass's annual report.
notes: Low profile and not an executive of the listed company. He holds a Hong Kong (non-permanent) resident ID. Not to be confused with SenseTime co-founder Xu Bing (徐冰). The route is via the Compass securities office.

name: Ren Luozhong
current_role: Vice chairman of Hangzhou Robam Industrial Group (Robam Appliances' controlling shareholder); chairman of the Yuhang (now Linping) District Robam Appliances Charity Foundation; chaired Robam's supervisory board 2023-Aug 2026
profile: Ren Luozhong (任罗忠), born 1962, is a long-time co-builder of Robam (老板电器), the Hangzhou kitchen-appliance maker known for range hoods. He started in 1982 at the Yuhang Hongxing hardware factory that became Robam and held sales, technology and production roles before serving as director, vice president and supervisory-board chairman of the listed company.
interesting_fact: Robam traces back to the Yuhang Hongxing Hardware Factory near Hangzhou and became one of China's best-known range-hood brands. In Aug 2026 founder Ren Jianhua handed the chairmanship to his son Ren Fujia.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the Yuhang Hongxing Hardware Factory in 1982 as an 'operations factory director'. He later headed both Robam Group's marketing centre and its technology centre, and he chairs the Yuhang District Robam Appliances Charity Foundation.
notes: His supervisory-board term ended 17 Aug 2026, and he isn't named in the 2025 annual report's officer list, so his listed-company role may have lapsed. Low media profile; Robam's chairman is now Ren Fujia. Route via Robam IR or the charity foundation.

name: Sun Weiting
current_role: Chairman of Huafu Fashion Co. (SZSE: 002042) and of parent Huafu Holding
profile: Sun Weiting (孙伟挺), born 1963, founded Huafu in 1993 with co-founder Chen Lingfen, with whom Hurun lists his wealth as shared. Huafu is one of the world's largest makers of colour-spun (melange) yarn and supplies global apparel brands. It now runs a 'cotton to sock' supply chain including Xinjiang cotton operations, and he has chaired the listed company since Dec 2008.
interesting_fact: Huafu describes itself as one of the world's largest colour-spun yarn makers. It says it holds the most patents in the colour-spun yarn industry and is the yarn of choice for major global apparel brands.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Huafu, he was a government official: textile-company planner (1982-87), deputy director at Zhejiang's Light Industry Department (1987-90), and deputy head of Shaoxing's Yuecheng District (1990-93). He started the company in 1993.
notes: Co-actual controller with co-founder Chen Lingfen (vice chairman and president), with whom Hurun shares the wealth listing. The textile business has limited overlap with energy or data centers. Route is via the board office.

name: Kamal Anthony Hatoum
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO of BBB Foods Inc. (NYSE: TBBB), operator of Tiendas 3B, Mexico City
profile: K. Anthony Hatoum, 62, founded Tiendas 3B, Mexico's leading hard-discount grocery chain, opening its first store in Mexico City in Feb 2005. He is a former J.P. Morgan banker, McKinsey engagement manager and Merrill Lynch PE managing director. He took BBB Foods public on the NYSE in Feb 2024, and by end-2025 it had 3,346 stores, 20 distribution centres and ~29,000 employees.
interesting_fact: The 3B model was inspired by Turkish hard discounter BIM, which he covered at Merrill Lynch. He weighed markets in Asia, Eastern Europe and Latin America before picking Mexico, and the chain's first private label (May 2005) was 'LactiBu' milk formula.
deep_cut_fact: Before Mexico he was a serial founder in Turkey, co-founding Advantage Card (credit card and loyalty program) and E-bebek, a baby-products retailer that was among Turkey's first online retailers. He holds civil engineering degrees from Columbia (BS) and MIT (MS) plus a Stanford MBA.
notes: Holds his stake via Bolton Partners Ltd. Strong entrepreneurship story (Turkey ventures, then Mexico) suited to the podcast. Best route is IR.

name: Dong Junzi
current_role: No current listed-company role found; former director and vice president of Yunnan Botanee Bio-Technology Group (SZSE: 300957), resigned March 2023
profile: Dong Junzi (董俊姿) is a co-founder of Botanee, maker of China's leading sensitive-skin brand Winona (薇诺娜). She joined in 2012, was director and VP from 2019, and led Winona's market-facing operations, especially its fast-growing online business, through the company's 2021 ChiNext IPO. She resigned all posts in March 2023 for personal reasons, and her current activities are not public.
interesting_fact: After the March 2021 IPO, Botanee briefly became the A-share cosmetics company with the largest market value, driven by Winona, which supplied about 90% of revenue.
deep_cut_fact: On Winona's rise she told CBNData: 'You have to do N things right to get to where we are today, not just one thing right.' On going global: 'Brands have no borders.'
notes: She left Botanee in 2023 and no current organisation or published contact was found. Botanee's IR email (ir@botanee.com) is not a route to her. On the Hurun U40 list (2021).

name: J. Jonathan Ayers
current_role: Director of FB Financial Corp. (NYSE: FBK) and FirstBank; CEO of Ayers Asset Management, Inc.; President of Ayers Real Estate Services, LLC
profile: Jon Ayers, 54, is the son of FirstBank founder Jim Ayers, who built a rural West Tennessee bank bought in 1984 into Nashville-based FB Financial. He began his career at FirstBank, has been on its board since 2000 and FBK's since 2017, and co-executes his late father's estate, which owns ~13.6% of FBK. He runs the family's investment office and a commercial real-estate firm.
interesting_fact: FirstBank grew from a small rural West Tennessee bank Jim Ayers bought in 1984 into FB Financial, an NYSE-listed bank holding company with about $17.1bn in assets and 91 branches (Q3 2026).
deep_cut_fact: Besides banking, he has held executive roles at two private tech companies, Group Data Services and Pro-Accura. In 2016 he formed Ayers Real Estate Services to invest in and manage commercial real estate. He chairs FirstBank's Trust Committee.
notes: Not to be confused with Jonathan W. Ayers, the former IDEXX CEO. The SEC 'TenPercentOwner' status reflects the family estate's holdings. Low public profile. FBK's media or IR contacts are the formal route, though he isn't an executive there. The Ayers Foundation is his family's philanthropy. Source for the 1984 bank purchase: https://www.knoxtntoday.com/firstbank-founder-has-died/

name: Will Roseff
current_role: Director of bet365 Group Ltd (Stoke-on-Trent) since September 2001
profile: William Wolfe 'Will' Roseff, born 1951, is a long-serving board director and early backer of bet365, the Coates family's Stoke-on-Trent online betting company. His fortune reportedly rests on a minority bet365 stake (one source says ~6.7%). The Sunday Times Rich List put him at £579m (254th) in 2025 and ~£591m (239th) in 2026.
interesting_fact: He is the lowest-ranked of the gambling-industry names on the Sunday Times Rich List but one of only a handful of non-Coates individuals to have built a fortune on bet365.
deep_cut_fact: Companies House records show him appointed a director of bet365 Group on 25 September 2001, among its earliest board members in the year the online sportsbook launched. He remains an active director.
notes: Very private, with no interviews, social accounts or published personal contact found. bet365 publishes no press email; the only route is a formal letter to bet365 Group Ltd, Bet365 House, Media Way, Stoke-on-Trent ST1 5SZ (registered office per Companies House). Gambling is a sensitive topic for some podcast audiences. Some outlets spell his name 'Rosseff'.

name: Xia Guoxin
current_role: Founder and Chairman of Shenzhen Ellassay Fashion Co. (SSE: 603808); Chairman of the China Fashion Designers Association
profile: Xia Guoxin (夏国新), a trained designer, founded the Shenzhen women's fashion brand Ellassay (歌力思) in the 1990s and built it into a multi-brand high-end group. He co-controls it with Hu Yongmei, with whom Hurun lists the wealth as shared. Besides Ellassay, the group owns or operates international labels including France's IRO, the UK's self-portrait, Laurèl and Canada's nobis.
interesting_fact: Ellassay's growth now leans on imported designer brands: by 2025 the UK label self-portrait had 78 stores in China with revenue nearing RMB 600m, and France's IRO had 70.
deep_cut_fact: He studied product design (BA) and fashion (MA) at Tianjin Polytechnic University, where he is now a guest professor. He chairs the China Fashion Designers Association and is a professor at Shenzhen University's art school.
notes: Strong design-entrepreneur story, but the fashion business has little energy or data-center overlap. Visible in industry circles through the designers association. Route is via the securities office.

name: Ge Yiyang
current_role: No current public role found; former chairman of DaFa Properties Group (ex-HKEX: 6111), resigned 2024
profile: Ge Yiyang (葛一旸) is the son of Shanghai developer founder Ge Hekai. He took over DaFa Properties' management around 2015 and, as chairman, led its 2018 Hong Kong IPO and its fast-turnover growth strategy. DaFa was later wound up by the Hong Kong High Court (Oct 2024) and delisted, and he had resigned as chairman by mid-2024.
interesting_fact: He rang the HKEX listing bell for DaFa Properties in 2018 as chairman after taking over the family developer from his father.
notes: DaFa defaulted on bonds in 2023, received a winding-up order in Oct 2024 and is in liquidation, so his Hurun-era wealth is likely much reduced. No current organisation or published contact was found, and he is not a good podcast fit. Alive status is unknown simply because there is no recent coverage.

name: James M Zemlyak
current_role: President of Stifel Financial Corp. (NYSE: SF) since June 2014; COO and EVP of Stifel, Nicolaus & Company
profile: Jim Zemlyak, 66, is one of the long-time architects of Stifel's growth from a regional St. Louis broker into a major wealth-management and investment bank. He joined from Robert W. Baird in 1999 as CFO, a role he held until 2018, and has been COO of the broker-dealer since 2002 and company president since 2014. His wealth comes from Stifel stock accumulated over 25+ years.
interesting_fact: He served as Stifel's CFO for nearly two decades (Feb 1999-Aug 2018) through its run of acquisitions, including Thomas Weisel Partners and Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, which turned it into a national firm.
deep_cut_fact: Before Stifel he was CFO of Milwaukee-based Robert W. Baird & Co. (1994-99) and of Baird Financial Corp. He came to St. Louis in 1999, two years after Baird colleague Ron Kruszewski became Stifel's CEO.

public_contacts.value: Media contact: Neil Shapiro, (212) 271-3447 (no email published)

notes: Low-profile operator who rarely gives interviews. Stifel's press releases publish phone contacts only, no emails. Route via Stifel corporate communications.
